input: a recorded events export (deployments, changes, builds, failures) — the extractor reads the export and never calls an API live

keys.deployment-frequency: deployments per period; a re-run of the same environment at the same target sha is flagged and excluded
keys.lead-time-for-changes: median hours from change merged to the first deployment shipping it, 1 decimal
keys.change-failure-rate: verified failures detected in the period over deployments in the period, percent, 1 decimal
keys.mean-time-to-restore: median hours from failure detected to restored, 1 decimal

joins.deployment-to-change: a deployment lists the PRs its compare range says it ships; each must resolve to a change merged no later than the deployment (dora/dangling-join, dora/temporal-join-violation)
joins.deployment-to-build: each deployment's target sha must be observed by a successful CI run (dora/unbuilt-deployment)
joins.change-to-build: each merged change's merge sha must be observed by a CI run (dora/change-without-build)
joins.change-to-deployment: each merged change must be shipped by some deployment (dora/unshipped-change)
joins.failure-to-deployment: each failure must name an existing deployment (dora/dangling-failure-join)
joins.failure-to-restore-evidence: each failure's mode must be in the taxonomy and its evidence must check out (dora/unknown-failure-mode, dora/unevidenced-failure, dora/restore-before-detection)

taxonomy.revert: service restored by reverting the change; evidence: revertPr — a change merged inside the incident window
taxonomy.rollback: service restored by rolling back to an earlier deployment of a different target sha; evidence: rollbackTo
taxonomy.hotfix: service restored by shipping a fix forward; evidence: hotfixPr — a change merged inside the incident window

re-run-rule: two deployments of the same environment at the same target sha are one deployment: the later row is a re-run mislabeled as a new deployment — flagged (dora/re-run-mislabeled) and excluded from every count
periods: day (yyyy-MM-dd), week (ISO week, keyed by its Monday), month (yyyy-MM); a period appears in the series when it has at least one deployment
trend-policy: trends, not scores: the series carries this definition version, never a benchmark label
